title: Conjectural Topological Decomposition of Mass
html:
Proposition. Conjectural Topological Decomposition of Mass

The mass \mathfrak{m}(\varrho) of a vortex in any quantum observable universe (mass identity) decomposes as a sum of a descended holonomy contribution and finitely many transient contributions localised at the exceptional divisors of the brane boundary (brane boundary):

  \mathfrak{m}(\varrho)
  = 
  \bigl\lVert\mathrm{Hol}_{\nabla_A}(\varrho_0;\mathfrak{G})\bigr\rVert
  + 
  \sum_{i=1}^{N}
  \bigl\lVert\Phi_q(z_i)\bigr\rVert,

where \Phi_q(z_i) gives the quantum dilogarithm (quantum dilogarithm) evaluated at the i-th blow-up centre z_i, and \varrho_0 forms the unknot core of \varrho.

Relationship to the proved theorem

We proved the analogous decomposition for morphisms supported along the recursive brane tower (recursive brane tower) as Topological Decomposition of Mass. That theorem uses the descent involution \hat\tau_n and Frobenius categorical traces to split \mathfrak{m}(\varrho) into descended and transient parts.

The present conjecture concerns the vortex case: \varrho forms a closed cycle whose support does not necessarily factor through a finite brane-tower extension. The holonomy \mathrm{Hol}_{\nabla_A} along \varrho_0 (the flat gauge-field holonomy of the base-level connection) replaces the descent-trace part. The quantum-dilogarithm sum captures the transient blow-up contributions at the exceptional divisors of the brane boundary \partial A.

Archimedean specialisation. What follows sits on the archimedean side of the substrate wall. It invokes real- or complex-analytic constructs: real-valued physical observables, real-analytic bounds, transcendental constants, or numerical evaluation at the substrate parameter q_0. Any generic categorical / q-deformation identities it draws on remain valid over an abstract coefficient ring; only their archimedean realisation is specialised here.
